shifts.summary: The exam was overall easy to moderate with most candidates attempting 77 to 89 questions well. Reasoning was generally easy, while quantitative aptitude leaned moderate. General awareness was easy for many, and English was easy overall. Time management and the new sectional timer were common concerns.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Candidates reported many statement‑based and matrix questions, with no clock or mirror types. Reasoning was generally easy, some found it very easy.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GK mix included current affairs and static topics, candidates found it easy overall.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quant was moderate overall, with many circle and trigonometry questions; time management was noted as a concern.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was easy for most candidates, with grammar and active‑passive questions common; passages were moderate in length.

asked.q: Tagore wrote a national song for Bangladesh

observations: Candidates noted time management was a challenge, especially in math and reasoning sections.
The paper pattern remained similar to previous years with no major changes.
A 15‑minute sectional timer caused difficulty for many candidates.
Overall attempts were high, with many reporting 85‑89 well‑attempted questions.
disagreements: Overall difficulty was split between Easy to Moderate (3 reports) and Moderate (3 reports).
Quant difficulty was reported as Easy by three sources and Moderate by six sources.

intro: The SSC CGL Tier 1 exam held on 7 October 2026 was conducted in three shifts. Shifts 1 and 2 have been reported, while shift 3 is still pending and its analysis will be added after the shift concludes. The difficulty levels varied from easy to moderate across sections, and the number of correctly attempted questions reported (77‑89 for shift 1 and 70‑86.3 for shift 2) are unofficial figures; SSC normally normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was described as easy to moderate, with reports differing, while shift 2 was largely reported as easy. The pending shift 3 has no difficulty rating yet.

faqs.q: How many questions were candidates able to attempt correctly on average in the reported shifts of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: In shift 1, candidates generally attempted between 77 and 89 questions well, and in shift 2 the range was 70 to 86.3 questions. These figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: Which sections were considered easy or moderate in the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: Reasoning was mostly easy, quantitative aptitude leaned moderate, general awareness was easy for many, and English was reported as easy overall across the reported shifts.

faqs.q: Was there any notable issue with time management in the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: Yes, candidates across the reported shifts highlighted concerns about time management, especially with the introduction of a new sectional timer.

faqs.q: When will the analysis for the pending shift of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 7 October 2026 be available?
faqs.a: The analysis for shift 3 will be added a few hours after the shift ends, once sufficient candidate reviews are collected.
